findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [object Object] as property keys and strips expiry fields
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` call `Object.prototype.toString()` on Zod schema instances, which both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`. The second computed property overwrites the first, and because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` neither validates that a numeric expiry field exists nor preserves expiry fields such as `expires_in` or `expiry_date` in `refreshTokenResponse.data`. Downstream callers that read `expires_in` or `expiry_date` from the parsed result (e.g. Zoom and Office 365) will get `undefined` / `NaN`.

findings.title: Defaulting missing refresh_token to literal "refresh_token" overwrites valid stored refresh tokens
findings.body: Lines 25-27 set `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever the refresh response omits `refresh_token`, even when credential sharing is disabled. For providers like Office 365 where the refresh response may omit `refresh_token` (`refreshTokenResponseSchema` defines `refresh_token: z.string().optional()`) and the parsed data is merged onto the existing credential (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), this overwrites the user's real `refresh_token` in the database with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, breaking future token refreshes.

findings.title: GoogleCalendarService saves the SafeParseReturnType wrapper object into credential.key and fails on fetch Response
findings.body: There are two bugs in `refreshAccessToken`: (1) `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed credential object that `googleCredentialSchema.parse()` previously returned. Passing `key` directly to `prisma.credential.update` overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: ... }`, which causes `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw on all subsequent requests even when credential syncing is disabled. (2) When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` object rather than a Gaxios response with `.data`, so `const token = res?.data` on line 94 is `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws a `TypeError`.

findings.title: Missing prisma import, missing refreshOAuthTokens call, and stale accessToken used in SalesforceCalendarService
findings.body: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`: (1) line 96 calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `prisma` is not imported in this file, causing a build error and runtime `ReferenceError`; (2) line 75 calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping the request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce token refreshes never use `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`; and (3) after refreshing the token, line 106 passes the old `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection` instead of `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: BiginCalendarService passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens and expects an Axios response
findings.body: In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, line 93 passes `credentialId` (the primary key of the credential row) as the third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of `credential.userId`, sending the wrong ID as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. Additionally, the `refreshFunction` callback returns an Axios response (`{ data: ... }`), whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when credential syncing is enabled, so `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)` on line 96 will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

findings.title: ZohoCrmCalendarService expects an Axios response object from refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: In `ZohoCrmCalendarService`, the `refreshFunction` callback passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` uses `axios` and returns `{ data: ... }`, but when credential syncing is enabled `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` object where `.data` is `undefined`. Accessing `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on line 217 will throw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

findings.title: HubspotCalendarService treats the fetch Response from refreshOAuthTokens as a parsed HubspotToken
findings.body: When credential syncing is disabled, `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken` resolves to a parsed `TokenResponseIF` object (`{ accessToken, expiresIn, ... }`). When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns an unparsed `fetch` `Response` object. Lines 192-202 then read `.expiresIn` and `.accessToken` directly off the `Response` instance (both `undefined`), resulting in `expiryDate: NaN`, persisting the raw `Response` object into `credential.key`, and passing `undefined` to `hubspotClient.setAccessToken`.

findings.title: Zoom adapter passes "zoomvideo" instead of app slug "zoom" to refreshOAuthTokens
findings.body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` (the directory name) as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, whereas Zoom's app slug in the database and in `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` is `"zoom"`. The sync endpoint will receive `appSlug=zoomvideo` instead of `zoom`.

findings.title: Webex adapter validates synced refresh responses against full webexRefreshedTokenSchema
findings.body: In `webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validates the response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`, any response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` containing only the access token and expiry will fail validation and reject with `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`.

findings.title: LarkCalendarService deletes synced credentials lacking refresh_token and parses sync responses with handleLarkError
findings.body: In `LarkCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, lines 61-64 delete the credential and throw if `refresh_expires_date` is expired or `refresh_token` is missing, line 66 requires a Lark `appAccessToken` even when delegating to the sync endpoint, and line 84 parses the response with `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` (which requires Lark's `{ code: 0, data: { access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, refresh_expires_in } }` payload) instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`.
